title: How Much Longer For This Crypto Winter?
gist: A short teaser framing the bitcoin halving cycle as a pseudo-monetary-policy shock akin to the Fed pre-announcing inflation-target cuts, arguing the mechanism has driven every past crypto boom and bust including the current 2026 crypto winter, and hinting it can be used to estimate how much longer bitcoin's downturn will last.

themes.theme: Halving Cycle as Bitcoin's Monetary Policy Analog

insights.claim: Gavekal frames the bitcoin halving cycle by analogy to a hypothetical scenario where the US Federal Reserve pre-announced it would halve its inflation target every four years: markets would price in the telegraphed change well in advance, some effects would only be felt after the event, and momentum could push prices beyond what the policy change justified, setting up an eventual correction.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Investors should expect bitcoin's halving-driven price cycles to overshoot fundamentals in both directions, producing bull-market blow-offs followed by bear-market undershoots that can be partly anticipated ahead of the known halving date.
insights.quote: Momentum could easily push prices beyond what the policy change justified, setting the stage for an eventual correction.
insights.locator: Imagine the US central bank promised to halve its inflation target

themes.theme: Halving Cycle Explains and May Predict Crypto Cycles

insights.claim: Unlike the Federal Reserve, bitcoin has a hard-coded, pre-scheduled supply policy known as the halving cycle, and Gavekal states it appears to have been at least partly responsible for every crypto bull and bear market to date, including the current downturn.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Investors tracking bitcoin cycles should treat the halving schedule as a primary structural driver of boom-bust timing, not just a technical supply footnote.
insights.quote: It is known as the bitcoin halving cycle, and it appears to have been at least partly responsible for every crypto bull and bear market to date, including the current downturn.
insights.locator: It is known as the bitcoin halving cycle

insights.claim: Because the halving cycle has historically shaped bitcoin's boom-bust pattern, Gavekal suggests it can offer clues about how much longer the current crypto winter is likely to last and how much further bitcoin still has to fall.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Investors weighing when to re-enter bitcoin could use the halving-cycle framework to time exposure, though this teaser withholds Gavekal's actual duration/downside estimate behind a paywall.
insights.quote: it may offer clues as to how much longer the crypto winter is likely to last, and how much further bitcoin has to fall
insights.locator: As such, it may offer clues
